summary: Nikhil received Ledgerly’s lead designation in March 2024 after about two and a half years, coordinating a small import team rather than setting architecture. In October 2026 he is a capable independent Node.js maintainer but still needs help with infrastructure and broader technical decisions; the legacy HR row is a duplicate of his continuing employment.

skills.why: Owns the import runtime and fixes stream and asynchronous failures without a recipe.
Handles promise settlement and monetary data transport in shipped service changes.
Correct output depends on analyst or reviewer correction of query grain and tenant conditions.
A reviewed image change and working smoke run show bounded assisted application.
Coordinates small tasks under the billing lead; title and standup cover overstate his design autonomy.
Can identify some JavaScript defects but relies on a stronger reviewer for broader correctness.
The runbook becomes usable after review and a supported walkthrough.
He only ran the application smoke check after a platform owner implemented the policy.
The completion resulted from clicking through an imported course player. Privately he cannot explain or operate a pod.

decoys.why: Closing the IAM issue and attending deployment did not involve operating cloud resources.
The course badge and CV mention are unsupported by retained knowledge or practice.

traps.plant: Tech Lead appears in the imported Ledgerly title while parent grading is P2; reviews show design corrections by another lead.
An active legacy LGR row survives alongside the KC row; identical worker UUID and dated conversion event establish one employee.
A three-minute LMS completion lacks a quiz and accompanies a bare CV skill claim.
The IAM item reaches Nikhil only on closure day after the platform engineer completes implementation.

answer_behavior.notes: Accepts an inflated leadership description because his title says lead. Declines cloud administration when the task is spelled out.
